StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Single, sim does not override on_stack, so it adds -- matching PowerCmd.ModifyAmount (PowerCmd.cs:236). The Amount IS read here (it is the reattach heal, ReattachPower.cs:47 / powers.py:2365-2366), which is precisely why leaving on_stack alone matters; monsters/hive/decimillipede.py applies it once per segment.

AfterDeath.rationale: The one unit in this family the sim gets STRUCTURALLY right: it uses the real after-death hook (hooks.on_death, cmds.py:105) plus should_remove_from_combat_after_death, so the segment genuinely dies at 0 HP and is retained, exactly as C# does -- and combat.py:288-292's comment says so outright ("a corpse the combat retained (a withered Decimillipede segment) keeps taking turns -- that is how it reaches REATTACH"). Guard-for-guard: `wasRemovalPrevented || base.Owner != creature` -> `creature is not self.owner or self.is_reviving` (powers.py:2347; see the wasRemovalPrevented guard below), and `!AreAllOtherSegmentsDead() || !base.Owner.IsDead` -> `if self._all_others_down(): return` (powers.py:2349-2350). The `|| !base.Owner.IsDead` arm is dropped, which is defensive only: on this path the owner is always dead. The else-branch (DoFadeOutOnAllSegments) is pure presentation.

ShouldAllowHitting.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: PowerCmd.apply now opens with `if not hooks.should_allow_hitting(target): return` (cmds.py:394-395), the sim's port of PowerCmd.Apply<T>'s `if (!target.CanReceivePowers) return null` (PowerCmd.cs:73-76), whose CanReceivePowers reuses Hook.ShouldAllowHitting (Creature.cs:308-322). ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDe.rationale: `creature != base.Owner -> true, else false` maps exactly to `return creature is not self.owner`. This is the only power in half B that uses the sim's real hook for it, and it is why the Decimillipede works: cmds.py:102-104 sets `retained_after_death = not should_remove_from_combat_after_death(...)` and combat.py:292 then keeps the corpse taking turns.

ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath.rationale: `ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath() => false`. C# strips a dead creature's powers at CreatureCmd.cs:533 (`creature.RemoveAllPowersAfterDeath()`, then each power's AfterRemoved) and this override opts out so the power survives the death it is supposed to react to. The sim never removes powers on death at all -- a grep of cmds.py's kill/death path finds no `powers.clear()` or per-power removal, and cmds.py:96-105 goes straight from the HP write to should_die / should_remove_from_combat_after_death / on_death -- so `false` is the sim's universal behaviour and this override is satisfied for free. Faithful HERE. The inverse is a real machinery gap owned by nobody: the C# DEFAULT is `true`, so every power WITHOUT this override should be stripped on its owner's death and in the sim none is. That is reported in content-power-report-b.md section 3 rather than verdicted on this unit, because it is an engine-wide absence and not this power's divergence. Third-file citations, not hashed here. ENGINE-LEVEL SIBLING (added 2026-07-26): the INVERSE finding -- that C#'s DEFAULT is `true` so every power WITHOUT this override should be stripped on its owner's death and in the sim none is -- now carries a verdict of its own at audit/records/seam/creature_card_cmds.json step 8b (`gap`, LIVE, executed on the Decimillipede). It used to exist only as prose in content-power-report-b.md section 3c. This entry stays `faithful` because the override asks for exactly the behaviour the sim gives for free; the engine-wide absence is step 8b's, not this unit's.

ShouldOwnerDeathTriggerFatal.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): `PowerModel.ShouldOwnerDeathTriggerFatal` EXISTS in the sim now. `Power.should_owner_death_trigger_fatal` defaults to True (PowerModel.cs:646) and the two non-mock overrides are ported at their own sites -- MinionPower unconditionally (MinionPower.cs:20-23) and ReattachPower as `_all_others_down()` (ReattachPower.cs:106-109, whose own comment says "shouldn't trigger fatal unless all other segments are dead too"). `cmds.should_trigger_fatal(target)` is the `Target.Powers.All(...)` test, and BOTH Fatal cards call it BEFORE their attack, which is where C# reads it and is load-bearing: the killing blow strips the very powers the test asks about (Creature.RemoveAllPowersAfterDeath). This is NOT death prevention -- the minion really dies -- which is exactly why the `is_dead` check both cards already had did not cover it. ReattachPower's override reuses the power's own `_all_others_down()`, which is `AreAllOtherSegmentsDead` -- so killing the LAST standing segment does trigger Fatal and killing any earlier one does not.  Pinned by test/test_card_residue_gaps.py.  NOT CLOSED: nothing at this site.  The text it replaced read: Same missing hook as MinionPower's, and here the override is CONDITIONAL: `ShouldOwnerDeathTriggerFatal() => AreAllOtherSegmentsDead()` (ReattachPower.cs:106-109), so killing a segment while others stand must NOT trigger a Fatal payoff and killing the last one must. The sim has no hook and cards/feed.py:45 tests only `target.is_dead`, which is True for a withered segment (it really sits at 0 HP -- the sim's own `_all_others_down` comment says so, powers.py:2334-2336). So Feed on a non-final segment grants +3 max HP in the sim and 0 in the game. LIVE by the same executed witness as power/minion's (Feed x a Minion-marked creature, delta 3 vs 0); reachability here is the ported Hive Decimillipede (monsters/hive/decimillipede.py) plus the ported Rare Ironclad Feed. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.rationale: CORRECTION worth writing down, because the parameter is misnamed in the decompiled source and the obvious reading is wrong: `wasRemovalPrevented: true` is passed when **Hook.ShouldDie returned FALSE**, i.e. when the DEATH was prevented (CreatureCmd.cs:566), and `false` on the path where the creature really dies (CreatureCmd.cs:519). It is NOT about ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath, which is computed separately at CreatureCmd.cs:508 and does not feed the flag. So `!wasRemovalPrevented` means "the creature actually died". The sim fires hooks.on_death ONLY on the should_die-returned-True branch (cmds.py:98-105) and fires nothing at all on the prevented branch (cmds.py:106-113 does hp = 1 then after_preventing_death), so every `!wasRemovalPrevented` guard in this batch is satisfied structurally rather than by a matching test. Faithful for every ported listener, because all of them early-out on the flag. The residue -- that the sim has no AfterDeath dispatch AT ALL for a prevented death -- is a dormant machinery gap: no ported power acts on `wasRemovalPrevented == true`. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

C# filters `GetTeammatesOf(Owner).Except([Owner]).Where(c => c.HasPower<ReattachPower>())` and asks `.All(s => s.IsDead)`; powers.py:2324-2336 filters `combat.enemies` for `e is not self.owner and "reattach" in e.powers` and asks `all(s.is_dead ...)`. Equivalent in single-player (teammates of an enemy == the enemy list), and the vacuous-truth case matches too: a lone segment gets `all([]) == True` on both sides, which is what makes killing the last one final.

powers.py:2359-2362 reproduces it, comment included. The heal differs in FORM -- C# calls `CreatureCmd.Heal(Owner, base.Amount)` (heal BY Amount, capped at max HP) where powers.py:2365-2366 SETS `hp = self.amount` -- but the segment is at 0 HP when it reattaches, so heal-by-N and set-to-N coincide. Recorded because they would not coincide if anything ever healed a withered segment first, and nothing does.

No C# counterpart is needed -- C# never removed the creature -- but the sim must clear the flag it set at cmds.py:102-104 or the revived segment would keep being treated as a corpse. Correct, and load-bearing.
